ui.title: Into the Edge
ui.question: Open question
ui.footnote: All images are scientific illustrations, not photographs.
ui.noWebgl: Into the Edge needs WebGL 2, which this browser does not provide.

drill.shareText: From a drill bit in your hand to the atoms of its coating.

0.name: Drill bit
0.caption: An ordinary drill bit. Its gold colour is not paint but a thin ceramic layer. Let's zoom in, all the way down to the atoms.

1.name: The tip
1.caption: The tip. Two cutting edges do all the work, pressing into metal under high force and heat.

2.name: Cutting edge
2.caption: Up close, the edge is not razor sharp. Its shape is prepared on purpose, because it decides how long the tool lasts.

2b.name: Ion-beam cut
2b.caption: To look inside, we cut a tiny trench with a beam of gallium ions.

3.name: Cross-section
3.caption: The coating is only a few micrometres thick. Below it, hard grains of tungsten carbide are held together by cobalt.

4.name: Columns
4.caption: The coating grows from a vapour, atom by atom, and forms tightly packed columns.

5.name: Nanolayers
5.caption: Inside, layers a few nanometres thick can alternate. Such stacks can be harder than either material alone.

6.name: Crystal lattice
6.caption: Titanium, aluminium and nitrogen in a cubic lattice, the same pattern as table salt. A coating holds thousands of these cells stacked up.

7.name: Atoms
7.caption: Atoms. The forces between them set every property of the coating. Today these forces can be computed with machine learning.

0.method: Monitoring of cutting force, power and acoustic emission.
0.question: The condition of a tool cannot yet be determined reliably from a single signal, and many methods remain confined to the laboratory.

1.question: Friction between the chip and the tool is poorly understood, and models simplify it heavily.

2.method: Calculation of stresses and temperatures at the cutting edge.
2.question: The main challenge is to link the calculated stresses and temperatures to tool wear.

3.question: The scratch test gives a semi-quantitative measure of adhesion; a true adhesion parameter usually cannot be obtained from it.

4.question: The diagrams give only an approximate picture, because more parameters affect coating growth than a diagram has axes.

5.question: The hardness of a thin coating depends on the indentation depth because of the substrate, and the “10% of the thickness” rule does not always hold.

6.question: When heated, the coating decomposes into nanodomains and becomes harder. How does this decomposition proceed under the combined heat and pressure of the cutting zone?

7.question: Conventional DFT is limited to about a thousand atoms. Universal ML potentials systematically underestimate energies and forces at surfaces, at defects and in high-energy states.

final.text: Linking these atomic forces to the life of a real tool is still an open problem. This is what I work on.
final.author: Pavel Peretyagin
